================================================================================
THIRD-PARTY NOTICES: dx, the Dioxus CLI, as shipped by CodeBrix.WebPlatform
================================================================================

This file travels with the `dx` program in the
CodeBrix.WebPlatform.FrontendBuilder.<Platform> packages (folder
frontend-tools/<rid>/ of a consuming build). It lists the third-party code
compiled into that program.

dx itself is the dioxus-cli crate, version 0.7.10, MODIFIED by seven patches
and used under the Apache License 2.0 (it is offered under "MIT OR
Apache-2.0"): see LICENSE-Dioxus.txt beside this file. Nothing listed below
is relicensed: every crate stays under its own license, and anyone who takes
one out of this program or out of the repository takes it under that
license. Where a crate offers a choice, its entry says which license it is
used under here.

ALSO IN THE PROGRAM, and not listed as crates below: the Rust standard
library of the Rust release that built it (pinned: 1.100.0), "MIT OR
Apache-2.0", https://github.com/rust-lang/rust - as in every Rust program.
The C code dx contains is compiled from crates listed below (ring, and the
zstd library bundled in zstd-sys, used under BSD-3-Clause).

LIBGIT2 IS NOT IN THE PROGRAM. dx links libgit2 1.9.7 as a SHARED LIBRARY
that it loads when it starts (libgit2-49e408b.so.1.9 on Linux,
libgit2-49e408b.1.9.dylib on macOS, git2-49e408b.dll on Windows); dx does not
start without it. That library is not part of this program or of this file:
it comes from the NuGet package CodeBrix.LibGit2.MitLicenseForever, which
carries libgit2's own licence (GPL-2.0 with the linking exception, and the
licences of the code bundled in it) beside the library. The crate
libgit2-sys listed below is the CodeBrix.WebPlatform repository's own
DECLARATIONS-ONLY stand-in (tools/dx-native-tools/sources/
codebrix-libgit2-sys): Rust declarations of libgit2's functions taken from
the crates.io crate libgit2-sys 0.18.3+1.9.2 ("MIT OR Apache-2.0"), with no
C code. Nothing from OpenSSL is compiled into or linked by dx: the
openssl-sys crate below is a dependency of git2 on Linux that the program
never uses (its declarations are not linked in), and libgit2 loads the
system's OpenSSL itself when it needs it.

THE BUNDLE SPLITTER IS MODIFIED. The crate wasm-split-cli listed below is
the crates.io crate wasm-split-cli 0.7.10 of the Dioxus project ("MIT OR
Apache-2.0", used under Apache-2.0) with two changes to its call graph made
by CodeBrix.WebPlatform; the patched source is in the repository's tool
sources (tools/dx-native-tools/sources/wasm-split-cli) and the changes are
recorded in tools/dx-native-tools/vendoring/wasm-split-cli.

MOZILLA PUBLIC LICENSE 2.0. Thirteen crates dx is built from are under the
Mozilla Public License 2.0 (smartstring declares "MPL-2.0+", version 2.0 or
later, and is used here under 2.0), whose full text is in the license texts at
the end of this file. Ten are compiled into dx and are listed below:
cssparser, cssparser-color, dtoa-short, lightningcss, nucleo, nucleo-matcher,
option-ext, parcel_selectors, smartstring and static-self. The other three -
cssparser-macros, lightningcss-derive and static-self-derive - are procedural
macros: they run while dx is compiled and generate code that is compiled into
it, but their own code is not in the program. dx contains all of this code in executable form,
UNMODIFIED. Their Source Code Form is available, unmodified and at no charge, in
the CodeBrix.WebPlatform repository
(https://github.com/ellisnet/CodeBrix.WebPlatform), in the tool vendor folder
named in the section below, one folder per crate and version
(<crate>-<version>/); it is also published on crates.io at the "Source" address
given in each entry. You may obtain it from either place.

CDLA-PERMISSIVE-2.0. The crate webpki-roots (the Mozilla root certificate
list) is under the Community Data License Agreement - Permissive 2.0; its
text is in the license texts at the end of this file.

THE CANIUSE DATABASE. dx contains browser-support data generated from the
caniuse database (https://github.com/Fyrd/caniuse, Copyright (C) 2020
Alexis Deveria, licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0
International licence, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/),
compiled in through the crate browserslist-data (which declares MIT and
records, in its src/generated/info.txt, that it was generated from caniuse
commit 7421f82105232274626207ff23f9ee03e6a7421c). The data was converted
into Rust tables by browserslist-data; CodeBrix.WebPlatform did not change
it.

APACHE-2.0 WITH LLVM-EXCEPTION. target-lexicon, wasm-encoder 0.214.0 and
wasmparser 0.214.0 are under the Apache License 2.0 with the LLVM Exception,
which only adds permissions to the Apache License 2.0.

ENTRIES WITHOUT "License files". Some crates, as published on crates.io,
carry no licence file (the entry then has no "License files" line). Their
declared licence is still the one shown; its standard text - the Apache
License 2.0, the MIT licence, the BSD 3-Clause licence, the Mozilla Public
License 2.0 - is among the license texts below, where another crate ships it.
For those crates no copyright line is known beyond the authors their
crates.io page names.

THIS FILE IS GENERATED. Everything after this opening is written by
`LibraryChecker notices --write` (libs/CodeBrix.WebPlatform.LibraryChecker)
from the license audit of what cargo compiles into dx on each of the five
platforms; this opening is tools/dx-native-tools/notices/
notices-header-Dioxus.txt. Edit the opening there, never the generated part.

================================================================================
Rust crates compiled into dx
================================================================================
Every crate cargo compiles into dx for at least one of the five platforms it is built for
(x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin).
A few are compiled in on some platforms only (operating-system bindings). Their source is in
the tool vendor folder of the CodeBrix.WebPlatform repository (tools/dx-native-tools/sources/vendor), unmodified;
the dioxus-cli source itself is beside it (tools/dx-native-tools/sources/dioxus-cli).

Mozilla Foundation is the license steward. Except as provided in Section
10.3, no one other than the license steward has the right to modify or
publish new versions of this License. Each version will be given a
distinguishing version number.

10.2. Effect of New Versions

You may distribute the Covered Software under the terms of the version
of the License under which You originally received the Covered Software,
or under the terms of any subsequent version published by the license
steward.

10.3. Modified Versions

If you create software not governed by this License, and you want to
create a new license for such software, you may create and use a
modified version of this License if you rename the license and remove
any references to the name of the license steward (except to note that
such modified license differs from this License).

10.4. Distributing Source Code Form that is Incompatible With Secondary
Licenses

If You choose to distribute Source Code Form that is Incompatible With
Secondary Licenses under the terms of this version of the License, the
notice described in Exhibit B of this License must be attached.
